mechanism_narrative: The recent rebound in WORKPLACES from -14.0 to -12.4 and TRANSIT remaining less depressed than earlier weeks indicates a modest return of weekday circulation. That should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as commuting-linked shopping and lunch trips recover.
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC does not rise above its prior 4-week mean despite WORKPLACES staying above -15 and TRANSIT not falling further.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated and WORKPLACES remains deeply negative, people substitute home-based activities for discretionary shopping, pushing RETAIL_REC lower within two weeks. The mechanism fails if this home-stay pattern weakens or retail visits stop tracking time spent at home.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above 7 while WORKPLACES stays below -10
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days while RESIDENTIAL remains above 7 and WORKPLACES remains below -10.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp deterioration in PARKS signals households shifting leisure time away from outdoor outings and toward indoor commercial venues, which lowers RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks. The signal is strongest after PARKS falls for two consecutive weeks by at least 5 points each week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by at least 5 points week-on-week for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC does not decline relative to the prior 4-week mean after the specified two-week PARKS drop.

mechanism_narrative: A broad mobility pullback across TRANSIT and WORKPLACES implies tighter restrictions or risk avoidance that suppresses discretionary trips immediately. Under that regime, RETAIL_REC should fall within one week and stay below its last-month average for the next month.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both drop below their previous-week levels
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC does not decline within 7 days after simultaneous week-on-week drops in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM rises while RETAIL_REC is still depressed, routine errand traffic is concentrating into essential trips rather than discretionary outings. That mix should keep RETAIL_REC from recovering over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM is above 2 for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days while GROCERY_PHARM stays above 2 for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES should amplify face-to-face commercial exposure, increasing retail visits over the next four weeks. The effect depends on both series moving upward together; one without the other will not produce the same retail lift.
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC fails to exceed its prior 4-week mean when both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES trend upward for at least two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The recent lift in PARKS alongside a recovery in RETAIL_REC indicates shared warm-weather or weekend-season activity. If PARKS remains above its earlier trough, retail and recreation should continue to improve over the next month.
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days while PARKS stays near or above its current level.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL remains elevated but TRANSIT and WORKPLACES stop falling, mobility is normalizing without a full return to discretionary outings. In that mixed regime, RETAIL_REC should be flat to slightly higher over the next two weeks, but only if the transit and work recovery continues.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES each stop declining for one week after being below -15
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC stays below its last 4-week average despite TRANSIT and WORKPLACES each stabilizing after prior declines.
